rv.q: This highly entertaining but nonetheless gentle show never preaches, never takes itself too seriously and embraces everyone in its orbit, all qualities that tend to lead to success in the theater.
The show took some of the most magnificent music ever written by an American composer, filtered it through a classic Shakespeare comedy and produced a first-rate show that does justice to both.
Krystal Joy Brown, in her role as the alluring, fragile diva Lady Liv, came out and set the theatre on fire and burned the whole place down.
We are in dark times and we need light, and love and joy and this show delivers.
This is one happy, hilarious musical that theatergoers will be flocking to see.
Epps's masterful direction blends exceptional music, soulful singing, energetic dancing, and witty comedic timing, making Play On! a show-stopping extravaganza of pure magic.
The joyful vibe generates a happy ending and an irrepressible smile.

The production is rousing and joyful, the music fits like a kid glove with the textual intentions, and the audience was filled with gasps and audible yesses throughout, showing that this exuberant celebration of Black jazz is “something to live for” and just what we need right now.

When the Rev (Alan H. Green, making a flawless transition from censor to libertine) comes out in a blindingly yellow suit to sing “I’m Beginning to See the Light,” he and the company blow the roof off the joint.
“Play On!” is lighthearted and rousing, guaranteeing you walk out of the theater happier than when you walked in.
The fusion of the Bard’s original romantic comedy with Duke Ellington’s songs and jazz compositions is nothing short of extraordinary!
With flamboyant music, fast-paced dancing and hearty comedy, Play On! proves to be an enjoyable start for their theatre season.

cn.t: Critics praise this Tony-nominated Twelfth Night adaptation for its brilliant fusion of Shakespeare and Duke Ellington's jazz, with standout performances (especially Hailee Kaleem Wright) and spirited 1940s Harlem setting delighting audiences.
